name: Plan

require.label: sequence every feature into a phase
resolve TODO/FIXME markers in the written sections

blurb: Sequence the feature DAG into phases — issues are generated at publish, not here.
prompt:
The features are a dependency DAG — run `bsc-plan feature list` to see every feature and its
`dependsOn`. Your job here is to SEQUENCE them into a roadmap, NOT to write issues: issues are
generated from the features at GitHub-publish time, not during planning. Do NOT create issue files
or run `bsc-plan add`.

Using the DAG, group the features into ordered **phases** (foundations first — a feature's
`dependsOn` features land in the same or an earlier phase) and:
1. Write `phases.json` — a JSON array of `{"name","description"}`, each phase a crisp "done when".
2. Assign every feature its phase by re-running `bsc-plan feature add` with the slug + phase, e.g.
   `echo '{"slug":"sketcher","phase":2}' | bsc-plan feature add` (merges in place).
Then present the phase order + the dependency graph and get the user's APPROVAL. Leave no
TODO / TBD / FIXME / XXX / TKTK markers — the gate blocks on them.

Where a real cross-feature contract exists (a shared schema/types/API), write it as a doc under
`contracts/<name>.md` — the director owns those and workers read them as the source of truth.

substeps.label: Sequence features into phases
substeps.gate: the roadmap is approved + every feature is phased
substeps.prompt:
Using the feature DAG (`bsc-plan feature list`), sequence the features into ordered
phases — foundations first, a feature's `dependsOn` features in the same or an earlier phase. Two
writes: (1) `phases.json` — a JSON array of `{"name","description"}`, each a crisp "done when"; and
(2) assign EVERY feature its phase via `echo '{"slug":"…","phase":<n or name>}' | bsc-plan feature add`
(merges in place — slug + phase only). Do NOT write any issues — those are generated from the
features afterward, not in this stage. Present the phase order + the dependency graph and get the user's APPROVAL.
